subject: general
question: Which type of Citizenship is provided by the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Single citizenship.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution of India gives **single citizenship** to the people of the country.
 
• All the people irrespective of the states or territories in which they reside are the citizens of the country.
 
• This is because India is a Union of states and not a federation. The states cannot separate from the Union.
 
• Unlike USA, where a citizen is a citizen of USA and the state in which he/she resides(dual citizenship).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Citizenship:**

 
• The Constitution of India provides for** single citizenship **for the whole of India.
 
• Every person who was at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950) domiciled in the territory of India, and
 
 
• **who was born in India**
 
• **Either of whose parents were born in India**
 
• **Who has been ordinarily resident in India for not less than five years, became a citizen of India.**
 
 
 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955 **deals with matters relating to acquisition, determination, and termination of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.
